title: Toward Automated Precision Tuning of Weather and Climate Models: A Case Study
problem: Floating-point precision tuning requires searching mixed-precision design spaces to identify computations amenable to reduced precision in complex weather and climate models while maintaining correctness. Prior approaches rely on tedious manual efforts by domain experts or use low-precision emulation that obscures actual speedup potential.
motivation: Weather and climate models are computationally intensive and complex, making them prime targets for precision tuning to achieve performance improvements at scale.
method: A bespoke Fortran transformation tool automates precision tuning by systematically searching the mixed-precision design space to identify and evaluate program variants that maximize performance subject to correctness constraints. The tool is applied to computational hotspots across three real-world weather and climate models (MPAS-A, ADCIRC, MOM6), replacing manual domain-expert efforts with automated performance-guided techniques.
key_novelty: First automated, performance-guided floating-point precision tuning case study at scale on real-world weather and climate models using a custom Fortran transformation tool.
contributions: First large-scale automated floating-point precision tuning study in weather and climate modeling
Bespoke Fortran transformation tool for automated precision tuning of large-scale scientific codes
Empirical evaluation and comparative analysis across three real-world operational weather and climate models
Best practices and lessons learned for feasible precision tuning in complex scientific computing domains

metrics.speedup: varying results across models (not quantified in abstract)

limitations: Limited discussion of generalizability beyond three specific models; scalability to other scientific domains not addressed.
primary_theme: automated floating-point precision tuning for weather and climate simulation
